Crystal Crop Protection financials show revenue growth and profitability trends over recent years, indicating business stability.

Crystal Crop Protection is an organization that provides crop solutions with agrochemicals and seeds being its key products. The company’s product lines include crop protection products such as herbicides, fungicides and insecticides, as well as natural crop solutions like bio-stimulants, bio-protectants, plant growth regulators, liquid fertilizers and micronutrients. Besides, it also provides seeds for field crops, vegetable crops and flowers.The firm provides more than 174 crop protection product brands available in various pack sizes, including farmer-friendly packs. Moreover, its branded crop protection business has been growing at a faster pace and the firm also exports formulations and technicals to many countries including Bangladesh, Nepal and parts of Africa and Asia. · · Its seeds business is diverse ranging from cotton, cereals, oilseeds, fodder crops, vegetables and flowers with presence not only across India but also through exports to countries such as Japan, the USA and Thailand.The firm runs various manufacturing units for formulations, technicals and seed processing in various locations including Haryana, Gujarat, Jammu & Kashmir, Maharashtra, Telangana and Karnataka. It has its R&D center in Sonipat, Haryana. · · Its business enjoys a strong network of around 13,000 distributors and 36 distribution centers spread all over India.
Nand Kishore Aggarwal, Ankur Aggarwal, Komal Aggarwal, Ankur Aggarwal KNK Family Trust are the company's promoters of Crystal Crop Protection.

b.p: Crystal Crop Protection Limited has allocated 49,98,708 equity shares to anchor investors at ₹272 per share, raising ₹135.96 crore ahead of its IPO. · · The allocation was made to 17 institutional investors, including Ashoka India Equity Investment Trust PLC, International Finance Corporation, WhiteOak Capital, Tata Mutual Fund, Silver Stride India Global Fund, Dharmayug Investments, Nomura Singapore and Citigroup Global Markets Mauritius. Crystal Crop Protection IPO - Strengths and Risks

b.p: Crystal Crop Protection IPO strengths and risks highlight key business factors, financial position, and market sentiment that may impact investor interest.

R&D Capability: The company follows an integrated R&D model of synthesis research in crop protection and natural crops along with seed breeding initiatives, which are further complemented by its GLP-accredited in-house research facility and nine field research stations, thus resulting in continuous launches of new products.

armer Connect and High Brand Equity: Several decades of interaction with the farming community have led to high brand equity with brands such as Bavistin having 100% recognition among surveyed grape farmers and brands such as Amora having 85% recognition in the herbicide category along with acquisition of famous brands such as Gramoxone and Furadan.

Pan-India Distributor Network: The company is able to reach farmers across India through its pan-India distributor network consisting of 13,285 independent distributors and 36 distribution centers in 23 states and four union territories.

Revenue Dependence on Domestic Crop Protection Products' Demand: Revenue earned from the operations depends significantly on domestic sales; crop protection products and natural crop solutions account for 77.82% of revenue for the first six months of fiscal year 2025, thus making the company susceptible to cyclicality in economic performance and demand within the Indian agrochemical sector.

Business Risk Related to Seasonality and Climate: The company operations, revenue, and working capital needs are seasonal in nature based on Kharif and Rabi cropping seasons, and bad or late monsoon, unusual weather patterns, or change in pest prevalence may significantly reduce the demand for formulations and seeds.

Dependency on Crop Protection Manufacturing Units: The business of the company is heavily reliant on six manufacturing plants for crop protection products and three plants for seeds processing; therefore, any unexpected disruption in these plants' operations due to mechanical breakdowns, labor issues, or natural calamities may affect revenue negatively.
